text:
Alyssa: Quick follow-up on the offload allocator RFC — want to align on a migration plan that avoids OOM regressions and reduces long-term fragmentation for multi-tenant hosts. Who's got time for a short plan?

Devon: I can. My rough idea: two-phase migration. Phase 1: compatibility shim that routes old allocator calls to the new backend with instrumentation. Phase 2: cutover/optimize and enable compaction heuristics. Metric-driven canary. :thinking_face:

Maria: FYI we already observed weird slab fragmentation when we moved pinned ranges to host backing in the earlier spike. Small allocations never consolidated. Example metric we saw: `evict_fragmentation_ratio` jumped 18% during the migration window.

Sam: Interface-wise I want an escape hatch: `Allocator.try_vacate(range) -> bool` plus `Allocator.retire(alloc_id)` so callers can opt into asynchronous vacates instead of blocking GC. If try_vacate returns false, callers can fallback to a soft-lease extend. Keeps latency bounded.

Devon: Agreed on non-blocking. Blocking vacates caused the latency spikes last time because of the syncpoint waits. Suggest `vacate_async(range, callback)` under the hood and a `vacate_token` we can poll. Pseudo: `token = vacate_async(r); if (!token.ready()) schedule_recompute();`

Alyssa: Important: we need a rollback signal. If fragmentation or OOM rate increases during canary, automatic fallback to the old allocator path. How do we detect regression cheaply?

Maria: Implement a cheap residency sampler + hotset estimator. Track `hotset_estimate` and `allocated_small_slab_pct`. If small slab pct increases > X for Y minutes, trigger rollback. Also expose `compact_priority` per-tenant so high-paying customers can opt-in to aggressive compaction.

Sam: Implementation detail: make `try_vacate` return immediately and record `vacate_attempts` metric. Then a background worker retries with exponential backoff up to N attempts. We should also emit `vacate_success_rate` and `max_blocking_wait_ms`.

Devon: For canary, propose rolling across hosts: start with 10 hosts, 48h stabilization, then 100 hosts, 72h, check metrics. If any host shows `stalled_evictions > threshold` or `fragmentation_pct` rising, abort and route traffic back. I'll draft the schedule.

offload-bot: Canary deploy started: allocator-shim v0.3 -> hosts [host-044..host-053], initiated by @Devon at 2026-03-21T15:05:30Z.

Maria: Also add a heartbeat metric from the vacate worker: `vacate_queue_len`. If queue grows > N we should stop new vacates and briefly increase soft-lease window to avoid thrashing.

Alyssa: Good. Can we add a small checklist in the RFC addendum: metrics to watch, per-tenant flags, rollback condition, expected perf delta? Keep it 1 page.

Devon: Will do. Items to include: `fragmentation_pct`, `stalled_evictions`, `vacate_attempts`, `vacate_success_rate`, `max_blocking_wait_ms`, `vacate_queue_len`, `hotset_estimate`. Also include recommended thresholds for canary.

Sam: One more: prefer API named `try_vacate` (no blocking) + `force_vacate` (admin only). Avoid exposing blocking semantics to serving paths.

Alyssa: SGTM. Devon, can you open the RFC addendum and assign owners for the telemetry + rollback runbook? I'll coordinate with infra on capacity for compaction.

Devon: Yup — opening addendum now and will ping for owners. Expect follow-up thread with concrete thresholds and test matrix. :thumbsup:

Maria: I'll start a small experiment harness to replay allocations and measure fragmentation under various vacate policies. Will post results here.

Sam: Thanks — sounds like a plan.
